findings.title: Heap buffer overflow due to wrong item_size in FT_ALLOC_MULT
findings.message: In commit bda1d87f694dd, the allocation for the `dists` array in `sdf_generate_bounding_box` was changed from `FT_NEW_ARRAY(dists, bitmap->rows * bitmap->width)` to `FT_ALLOC_MULT(dists, bitmap->rows, bitmap->width)`. The macro signature is `FT_ALLOC_MULT(ptr, count, item_size)`, which calls `ft_mem_realloc(memory, item_size, 0, count, ...)` — allocating `count * item_size` raw bytes. With the call `FT_ALLOC_MULT(dists, bitmap->rows, bitmap->width)`, the allocation is `bitmap->rows * bitmap->width` bytes total (treating each element as `bitmap->width` bytes wide). However, `dists` is typed as `SDF_Signed_Distance*`, a struct containing two `FT_16D16` (4 bytes each) and one `FT_Char` (padded to ~12 bytes). The correct size should be `sizeof(SDF_Signed_Distance) * bitmap->rows * bitmap->width`. The undersized allocation causes a heap buffer overflow whenever any element `dists[index]` is written (for indices 0..(rows*width-1)), since each write is ~12 bytes but only 1 byte per element slot was allocated. Additionally, `FT_ALLOC_MULT` does not zero-initialize memory, while the subsequent code checks `dists[index].sign == 0` as a sentinel — leading to uninitialized reads. The fix adds an explicit overflow guard on `bitmap->rows * bitmap->width` and reverts to `FT_NEW_ARRAY(dists, bitmap->rows * bitmap->width)` which correctly uses `sizeof(*dists)` as element size and zero-initializes the buffer.

location.snippet:
if ( FT_ALLOC_MULT( dists, bitmap->rows, bitmap->width ) )
      goto Exit;

findings.suggestion: Use FT_NEW_ARRAY(dists, bitmap->rows * bitmap->width) (which uses sizeof(*dists) as element size and zero-initializes) with an explicit integer-overflow guard before the multiplication. There is no FT_NEW_ARRAY_MULT macro in FreeType, so the guard must be added manually.

ground_truth.root_cause: The programmer used `FT_ALLOC_MULT(ptr, count, item_size)` with `bitmap->rows` as count and `bitmap->width` as item_size to avoid the unchecked integer overflow in the original `bitmap->rows * bitmap->width` multiplication. However, `FT_ALLOC_MULT`'s `item_size` parameter is a raw byte size — not an element count — so the total allocation became `bitmap->rows * bitmap->width` bytes instead of `sizeof(SDF_Signed_Distance) * bitmap->rows * bitmap->width` bytes. A macro `FT_NEW_ARRAY_MULT` (which would accept a count and auto-derive sizeof) does not exist in FreeType, so the correct fix is to add an explicit overflow check and fall back to `FT_NEW_ARRAY`.
